title: Impact of School Finance Reform on Math Test Scores

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
The research scenario is best suited for a Difference-in-Differences (DID) analysis. The key identifying assumption for DID is the parallel trends assumption. This assumes that, in the absence of the school finance reform, the treated and untreated (control) groups would have followed the same trend over time. By comparing the changes in outcomes over time between the two groups, we can isolate the causal impact of the reform.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read the dataset
file_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s35_data.csv"
data <- read_csv(file_path)

# Run a Difference-in-Differences regression
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated * post, data = data)

# Print the main coefficient of interest: the interaction between treated and post
did_summary <- coeftest(did_model, vcov = vcovHC(did_model, type = "HC1"))
coeff_impact <- did_summary["treated:post",]
print(coeff_impact)

# Robustness Check: Add control for periods
did_model_with_period <- lm(y ~ treated * post + factor(period), data = data)
did_summary_with_period <- coeftest(did_model_with_period, vcov = vcovHC(did_model_with_period, type = "HC1"))
coeff_impact_with_period <- did_summary_with_period["treated:post",]
print(coeff_impact_with_period)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect the sign of the causal effect (coefficient on `treated:post`) to be positive, indicating that the school finance reform leads to improved math test scores. The magnitude of this effect will depend on the intensity and effectiveness of the reform, but in standard deviation units of test scores, a substantial reform might lead to an increase between 0.1 and 0.3 standard deviations. This would reflect a meaningful improvement in educational outcomes due to increased financial support.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: We compare changes in math test scores over time between schools affected by the reform and those that were not.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The reform led to a decrease in math test scores.
